title:
Myanmar Rejects Parts of a Genocide Ruling.
South Korea Raises Rates Again.
A Blast Hits a Bangkok Refinery.
subject: Myanmar Rejects Parts of a Genocide Ruling. South Korea Raises Rates Again. A Blast Hits a Bangkok Refinery.
preview_text: A defiant Myanmar, a Seoul rate hike, a cheaper HIV jab, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: Myanmar defies parts of a genocide ruling, South Korea lifts rates to a two-year high and a fire hits a Bangkok refinery.
contents_extra: Why a cheap HIV prevention jab matters for Africa, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Myanmar Says It Will Defy Parts of the Genocide Ruling
paragraphs: Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing says the country will not comply with "inappropriate" parts of the genocide ruling, the BBC reports. It was his first public comment since the International Court of Justice decision last week. The court found Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in a 2017 crackdown. His statement did not say which parts Myanmar rejects.

AP reports he told a Cabinet meeting the government would reject measures it considered "inappropriate", citing the state-run Global New Light of Myanmar. The court ordered Myanmar to let the Rohingya return safely, pay reparations and prosecute suspects. Its rulings are final and binding. But it cannot enforce them beyond reporting noncompliance to the UN Security Council, AP says.

stories.title: South Korea Lifts Rates to a Two-Year High
paragraphs: CNBC reports South Korea's central bank raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 3.25% on Thursday. That is its highest level in two years. The Bank of Korea said inflation would stay above its 2% target for a considerable time. Inflation stood at 2.8% in October. The Kospi rose 1.88% after the decision, CNBC says.

AP reports the bank lifted its growth forecasts to 3.9% for 2026 and 4.1% for 2027. Booming semiconductor exports tied to AI demand have powered the economy. The bank warned rising house prices around Seoul could worsen household debt. Two of the seven policy committee members wanted to keep the rate at 3%, AP says.

stories.title: A Blast and Fire Hit a Bangkok Oil Refinery
paragraphs: The BBC reports seven people were injured, four critically, after an explosion at a Bangkok oil refinery on Thursday, citing local officials. The blast hit the Phra Khanong facility run by Bangchak Corporation at around 14:45 local time. The company said the fire was put out within 30 minutes. It said the cause was being investigated.

AP reports at least nine people were injured, three critically, citing Erawan Medical Center. A mobile phone alert told residents to avoid the area, and nearby residents were forced to evacuate. Video on social media showed thick black smoke over an eastern neighborhood. The refinery has a listed capacity of 120,000 barrels a day. It is Thailand's fifth biggest and the only one in an urban area, AP says.

deep_dive.title: Why a Cheap HIV Prevention Jab Matters for Africa
paragraphs: The Global Fund says the world's first deliveries of generic lenacapavir arrived in Zambia. A delivery to Uganda is expected in the coming days. Another shipment will arrive in Zimbabwe in early 2027. Lenacapavir is a twice-yearly injection. The Global Fund says it is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infections.

The price is the big change. The BBC reports the generic version is expected to cost just $40 per person a year. The original version from Gilead Sciences cost about $28,000 a year in the US. In a 2024 trial of more than 5,000 young women in Uganda and South Africa, none who got the injection contracted HIV.

AP reports the generic was developed by India-based Dr. Reddy's Laboratories under a deal brokered by the health agency Unitaid. The US Food and Drug Administration approved it earlier this month, but only tentatively. It cannot be sold in the United States while Gilead's patent stands. Gilead signed royalty-free licenses with six generic makers, AP says.

Scale is the next test. The Global Fund says more than 189,000 people in 10 early-adopter countries have had a first dose. With the US government, it aims to reach at least 3 million people by the end of 2028. The BBC notes concerns that US foreign aid cuts could undermine progress against HIV in Africa.

trivia.question: What is generic lenacapavir expected to cost per person each year?
trivia.explanation: The answer is $40. The BBC reports the original version cost about $28,000 a year in the US.

World view: A fuel tanker crash sets off a deadly fire in Cairo, the BBC reports Egypt's health ministry says 31 people were killed.
DR Congo summons Uganda's envoy over the army chief's posts, the BBC reports Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba appeared to back a rebel takeover.
Guinea orders a mass clean-up of Conakry, the BBC reports residents face a 31 December deadline.
Need to know: Kim Jong Un calls for a bigger nuclear arsenal, CNBC reports, citing North Korean state media.
North Korea expels Switzerland's diplomat in a sanctions row, the BBC reports the envoy was given 48 hours to leave.
A Hamas official and his wife are among eight killed in Gaza strikes, the BBC reports, citing local sources.
Money & markets: Global stocks rally while US markets close for Thanksgiving, CNBC reports European shares were sharply higher on Thursday morning.
K-beauty stocks jump on Amazon bestseller rankings, CNBC reports APR shares climbed 3.77% on Thursday.
New US tariff proposals may give India an edge, CNBC reports a proposed 17% rate if India finalizes a trade deal.
Future frontiers: US regulators approve SpaceX's million-satellite data plan, the BBC reports astronomers warned it could undermine their work.
Europe's largest satellite factory opens in Belgium, CNBC reports Aerospacelab will build 264 IRIS2 satellites.
Xpeng says home robots may be one to two years away, CNBC reports its co-president's comments.
The score: The Pittsburgh Steelers release Aaron Rodgers, BBC Sport reports he may have played his last NFL game.
Oliver Bearman stays with Haas for 2027, BBC Sport reports the deal was announced at the Qatar Grand Prix.
Manchester United draw a chaotic game in Lisbon, BBC Sport reports Pochettino is still waiting for a first win.
Life & culture: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65, the BBC reports his bandmates said he had prostate cancer.
India cancels screenings of a hit Pakistani TV drama, the BBC reports two Bengaluru events were called off after a backlash.
A motorcycle passenger's one-handed cricket catch goes viral, BBC Sport reports Mehran Khan took it in Pakistan.
